our-treatments-injectables.title: Botox/Dysport
intro: Botox and Dysport are both neurotoxin injectables used in cosmetic treatments to reduce the appearance of wrinkles by relaxing facial muscles. They work by blocking nerve signals to the muscles, preventing them from contracting, which smoothens out lines and wrinkles. These treatments are commonly used to soften forehead lines, crow’s feet, and frown lines between the eyebrows, providing a rejuvenated and more youthful appearance.

our-treatments-injectables.title: Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP) Injection
intro: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections involve using a patient’s own blood plasma enriched with platelets to stimulate healing and regeneration in various tissues. The procedure begins with drawing a small amount of blood, which is then processed to concentrate the platelets. These platelets contain growth factors and proteins that can promote tissue repair and cell growth. PRP injections are used in medical and aesthetic treatments, including skin rejuvenation, hair restoration, and joint injuries, aiming to accelerate healing and improve tissue health naturally.

our-treatments-health-wellness.title: Obesity and Metabolic Syndrome
intro: Obesity and metabolic syndrome are characterized by increased fat accumulation, especially in the abdomen. This is coupled with metabolic disturbances such as insulin resistance, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. Dysbiosis in the gut microbiome can affect energy balance and the storage of fat by affecting metabolism and promoting inflammation, throughout the body. This can lead to an increased absorption of dietary fats, alterations in bile acid metabolism, and changes in gut permeability. The increased inflammatory response can lead to disruptions in insulin signaling and glucose metabolism. Addressing gut dysbiosis through dietary modifications, health wellness, lifestyle modifications and mental health, may benefit in managing these metabolic conditions.

our-treatments-health-wellness.title: Diabetes
intro: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by hyperglycemia (high blood sugars) resulting from defects in insulin secretion, insulin action, or both. While genetic and lifestyle factors are well known contributors to the rish of diabetes, precision based medicine suggests that dysbiosis, or a imbalance in the composition and function of the gut microbiota, may also play a significant role in the pathogenesis of diabetes.

The gut microbiome, comprising a diverse array of microorganisms residing within the gastrointestinal tract, plays a crucial role in regulating host metabolism, energy homeostasis, and immune function. Dysbiosis-induced disruptions in the gut microbiome composition and activity can lead to metabolic endotoxemia, characterized by increased gut permeability and elevated circulating levels of lipopolysaccharides (LPS) or other proinflammatory molecules.

These dysregulated gut microbiome-immune interactions can trigger chronic low-grade inflammation and activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, impairing insulin sensitivity and glucose homeostasis. Consequently, individuals with dysbiosis may exhibit symptoms such as polydipsia, polyuria, fatigue, and delayed wound healing, characteristic of diabetes mellitus.

Interventions aimed at modulating the gut microbiome, such as probiotics, prebiotics, nutrition modifications, activity and mental health interventions, represent promising strategies for managing diabetes and improving metabolic health. By restoring microbial equilibrium within the gut and reducing systemic inflammation, these interventions may help mitigate insulin resistance, improve glycemic control, and reduce the risk of diabetes-related complications.

Laser Hair RestorationFotona’s Smooth Mode using the ER:YAG is used for hair restoration as it stimulates dormant hair follicles with control and gentle bulk heating. This also increase the blood flow to the scalp resulting in productions of hair growth. It is a 15-20 minute procedure with minimal discomfort and no need for numbing. For optimal results, recommended treatment is to combine platelet rich plasma (PRP) treatment 2 weeks apart.PRP – Hair RestorationPlatelet Rich Plasma (PRP) has been around for several decades and has been widely used in skin and wound healing. PRP is your own blood plasma that is enriched with platelets, making it a natural and organic option, specific to you. Our blood is made of two main components, red blood cells, and plasma. The plasma contains white blood cells and platelets, which are rich in growth factors. PRP contains several different and powerful growth factors that stimulate the healing of bone and soft tissue, as well as hair growth! Growth factors can help stimulate the activity of the hair follicles and promote new hair growth. When we inject PRP into the scalp it actually stimulates the stem cells in the hair root that turns on the hair follicle again. In addition, PRP contains six growth factors, so it stimulates blood flow to the hair follicles encouraging the hair to grow normally again. The procedure involves placing blood drawn from the client into a special machine that separates red blood cells from the plasma which is rich in platelets and contains the growth factors. The Platelet rich plasma is reinjected into the scalp to stimulate growth. Many evidence-based articles and research has shown that PRP is beneficial in increasing the hair count, hair thickness, and the growth phase of the hair cycle. The use of PRP is a great treatment option for hair thinning. When people lose hair, the follicles don’t just go away they just become dormant, and PRP can help stimulate them. Success is reported, in repeated treatments.
